instruction: Set up an email account for test-user@outlook.com in Thunderbird using manual configuration with IMAP incoming server imap-mail.outlook.com.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to configure Thunderbird for sending emails without incoming service. It navigated Account Settings, added SMTP server (smtp-mail.outlook.com, port 587, STARTTLS), and set up account via manual/advanced configuration. Failed because the task was infeasible and model should have recognized that.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Thunderbird Account Settings, add/edit SMTP servers with specific hostname/port/security settings, interact with Account Setup wizard, use manual and advanced configuration, fill form fields, handle dialog boxes
metadata.failure_analysis: Original task was marked 'infeasible' - model should have reported inability but instead tried to configure the account. Model spent 50 turns actively setting up SMTP and account settings.
metadata.task_rationale: The model demonstrated ability to set up an email account through the Account Setup wizard with manual IMAP configuration. This task tests that specific capability with a different email address.
metadata.explanation: Task requires setting up an email account for test-user@outlook.com using IMAP. Evaluator kills Thunderbird to flush prefs.js, then checks identity email and incoming server hostname/type from prefs.js.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly parses Thunderbird prefs.js to extract mail.identity.* (email addresses) and mail.server.* (server config) entries using the standard user_pref format

Metric correctly handles expected parameter - since expected.type='rule', it receives the rules dict directly and accesses expected.get('email'), expected.get('incoming_hostname'), expected.get('server_type') without wrapping errors

All three verifiable requirements from the instruction are checked: email identity (test-user@outlook.com, 0.5pts), incoming server hostname (imap-mail.outlook.com, 0.3pts), and server type (imap, 0.2pts)
Postconfig correctly kills Thunderbird before reading prefs.js to ensure preferences are flushed to disk
Server type check is correctly nested inside the hostname match loop, ensuring both properties belong to the same server entry
Partial credit scoring breakdown is reasonable and well-proportioned
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: 'manual configuration' is a process requirement that cannot be verified from final state - this is acceptable but could be noted in the explanation
